```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

## Use the synthetic fixture

`nis_example()` creates an invented Parquet dataset with familiar NIS fields.
It is suitable for learning and examples, not for estimating national
quantities.

```{r fixture}
path <- nis_example(years = 2019:2020)
nis <- nis_open(path)
nis |> dplyr::count(YEAR) |> dplyr::collect()
```

The result reports the number of synthetic rows in each selected year.

easyNIS does not bundle real NIS data. The HCUP [Nationwide Data Use Agreement](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/team/NationwideDUA.jsp)
advises avoiding publication of values of 1–10 in text and tables. Separately,
the [Checklist for Working with the NIS](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/db/nation/nis/nischecklist.jsp)
says at least two hospitals must contribute to each cell. `nis_suppress()` masks counts at or below `threshold` (10 by default), applies
complementary suppression by default for data frames, and, when given hospital
counts from `nis_cell_counts()`, masks cells from fewer than two hospitals. Use
`nis_example()` to try the workflow without
licensed data.

## Select years and columns

`years` limits which annual files are opened. Use `dplyr::select()` to narrow
what a later collection needs; lazy operations are evaluated when collected.

```{r columns}
nis_open(path, years = 2020) |>
  dplyr::select(YEAR, AGE, FEMALE, LOS) |>
  dplyr::collect() |>
  head()
```

The preview contains only the requested variables from the synthetic 2020
file. Mixed-case column names are normalized to upper case; already lower-case
names remain unchanged.

## Filter and project before collecting

`nis_open()` uses DuckDB's native Parquet reader and returns a lazy dbplyr
table. `duckdb`, `dbplyr`, and `DBI` are required dependencies. Filter and
select before collecting when later analysis needs an in-memory data frame.

```{r duckdb}
duck <- nis_open(path, years = 2020)
duck |> dplyr::count(YEAR) |> dplyr::collect()
```

This count is the same synthetic year summary, evaluated through DuckDB.

When converting HCUP ASCII files to Parquet, declare the source encoding so
string values are written as valid UTF-8. For example, convert Latin-1 text to
UTF-8 rather than writing bytes under the wrong encoding label.

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - Opening all years and collecting all columns can require substantial
>   memory. Filter and select before collecting.
> - Survey-design preparation collects the selected design fields in R. Keep
>   the cohort and retained columns bounded before using `nis_design()`.
> - `nis_example()` data are invented and should not be reported as NIS
>   estimates.

See [Cohort definitions](cohorts.html), [`nis_open()`](../reference/nis_open.html),
and [`nis_example()`](../reference/nis_example.html).
